Run the full eSVD-DE pipeline on a Seurat object

Source: R/eSVD.R
eSVD.Rd

The end-to-end wrapper: format_covariates, initialize_esvd and two rounds of opt_esvd (the case-control coefficient held fixed, then freed), each of the three followed by reparameterization_esvd_covariates, estimate_nuisance, and then either the fused compute_test_per_gene (bool_diet = TRUE) or compute_posterior, compute_test_statistic and compute_pvalue in sequence.

Usage

eSVD(
  batch_var_prefix,
  case_control_levels,
  case_control_var,
  categorical_vars,
  id_var,
  numerical_vars,
  seurat_obj,
  alpha_max = NULL,
  bool_adjust_covariates = FALSE,
  bool_covariates_as_library = TRUE,
  bool_diet = TRUE,
  bool_intercept = TRUE,
  bool_library_includes_interept = TRUE,
  bool_stabilize_underdispersion = TRUE,
  bool_use_log = FALSE,
  cap_multiplier = 10,
  intermediate_save = NULL,
  k = 30,
  l2pen = 0.1,
  lambda = 0.1,
  library_min = 0.1,
  max_iter = 100,
  min_cells_per_individual = 3,
  pseudocount = 0,
  tol = 1e-06,
  verbose = 0
)

Arguments

batch_var_prefix

NULL, or a regular expression matched against the names of categorical_vars; the matching covariates are treated as batch variables and their coefficients are not reparameterized.

case_control_levels

Character vector of length 2 giving the two levels of case_control_var, control first, then case. Reversing them flips the sign of every test statistic.

case_control_var

Name of the column in seurat_obj@meta.data holding the case-control status.

categorical_vars

Character vector of column names in seurat_obj@meta.data to adjust for as factors (one-hot encoded, first level dropped), or NULL. A variable with a single level is dropped.

id_var

Name of the column in seurat_obj@meta.data naming each cell's individual (donor).

numerical_vars

Character vector of column names in seurat_obj@meta.data to adjust for as numerical covariates, or NULL. They are rescaled by format_covariates.

seurat_obj

A Seurat object whose "RNA" assay has a "counts" layer (genes by cells) and whose meta.data holds the variables above.

alpha_max

Maximum value of the prior mean in the posterior; NULL (the default) uses twice the largest count.

bool_adjust_covariates

See compute_posterior.

bool_covariates_as_library

See estimate_nuisance and compute_posterior.

bool_diet

If TRUE (the default), compute the posterior, test statistics and p-values one gene at a time without allocating cell-by-gene posterior matrices, and drop dat, covariates and the intermediate fits fit_Init and fit_First from the returned object. The final fit (fit_Second: x_mat, y_mat, z_mat, nuisance_vec) is kept either way.

bool_intercept

Whether the per-gene GLMs include an intercept.

bool_library_includes_interept

See estimate_nuisance.

bool_stabilize_underdispersion

See compute_posterior.

bool_use_log

See estimate_nuisance.

cap_multiplier

One positive number, default 10: no gene's nuisance rate may exceed this many times the median of its library size, and Inf means no cap. See estimate_nuisance. The factorization does not depend on it, so recompute_pvalue can change it afterwards without fitting again.

intermediate_save

NULL, or a file path at which the object is saved after each major stage.

k

Number of latent dimensions; must not exceed the number of genes.

l2pen

L2 penalty for opt_esvd.

lambda

Ridge penalty for initialize_esvd.

library_min

See compute_posterior.

max_iter

Maximum iterations for each opt_esvd call.

min_cells_per_individual

Minimum number of cells every individual must contribute; an individual with fewer is an error. 0 disables the check. See compute_test_statistic.

pseudocount

See compute_posterior.

tol

Convergence tolerance for opt_esvd.

verbose

Integer; 0 is silent.

Value

An eSVD object with elements teststat_vec, case_mean, control_mean, case_var, control_var, log2fc_vec and log2fc_se_vec (the log2 fold change and its standard error; see compute_log_fold_change), pvalue_list (see compute_pvalue), param, case_control, individual, latest_Fit and the fit it names (an eSVD_Fit with x_mat, y_mat, z_mat, nuisance_vec and the other per-gene vectors of estimate_nuisance), plus dat, covariates, the earlier fits and the posterior matrices when bool_diet = FALSE. param records the settings of every stage (the opt_* entries are those of the first opt_esvd call, because a later call does not overwrite an entry that is already there), the number of genes whose nuisance rate was capped (nuisance_num_capped) and the arguments of this call that name the variables (as esvd_*), which is what lets recompute_pvalue and plot_fitted_vs_observed rebuild the counts and covariates from seurat_obj alone. report_results turns the object into a data frame, and plot_nuisance and plot_fitted_vs_observed draw its diagnostics.

Details

This function refuses inputs the model cannot handle, rather than filtering them: a gene whose counts are all zero, an individual with fewer than min_cells_per_individual cells, or an arm with fewer than two individuals each produce an error naming the offending genes or individuals. The recommended entry point, eSVD_helper, applies the cohort filters and removes all-zero genes before calling this function, and reinserts the removed genes afterwards with a gene_status record. It does not refuse an underpowered cohort (few cells or few individuals overall); those minima are eSVD_helper's policy.

The model is a Gamma-Poisson hierarchy: \(A_{ji} \mid \lambda_{ji} \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\ell_{ji} \lambda_{ji})\) with \(\lambda_{ji} \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\mathrm{mean} = \mu_{ji}, \mathrm{var} = \gamma_j \mu_{ji})\), where \(\mu_{ji}\) is a low-rank function of the cell and gene latent vectors plus the case-control covariate, and \(\ell_{ji}\) is the covariate-adjusted sequencing depth. Note that the package stores the Gamma rate \(\beta_j = 1/\gamma_j\) as nuisance_vec, so larger values mean less over-dispersion. Differential expression is a difference in mean expression between the case and control individuals, tested with a Welch statistic on the per-individual posterior means. See Lin, Qiu and Roeder (2024) doi:10.1186/s12859-024-05724-7 .

Examples

# \donttest{
if(requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE)){
  set.seed(10)
  sim <- generate_null(cell_per_person = 15, num_genes = 40,
                       num_individuals = 8)
  meta_df <- data.frame(sim$covariates[, c("CC", "Sex", "Age")])
  meta_df$Sex <- factor(meta_df$Sex)
  meta_df$Individual <- sim$metadata_individual
  rownames(meta_df) <- rownames(sim$obs_mat)
  # Seurat rewrites "gene_1" as "gene-1" (with a warning); rename first
  count_mat <- Matrix::t(sim$obs_mat)
  rownames(count_mat) <- gsub("_", "", rownames(count_mat))
  seurat_obj <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(counts = count_mat,
                                                 meta.data = meta_df)

  esvd_obj <- eSVD(batch_var_prefix = NULL,
                   case_control_levels = c("0", "1"),
                   case_control_var = "CC",
                   categorical_vars = "Sex",
                   id_var = "Individual",
                   numerical_vars = "Age",
                   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,
                   k = 2,
                   max_iter = 5)
  utils::head(report_results(esvd_obj))
}
